rationale: Loom doctor's domain whitelist (behavior/ui/data/architecture/terminology) is requirement-kind only. Findings (kind=finding, domain=experimental) and process_rules (kind=process_rule, domain=operational) trigger spurious 'Non-standard domains' warnings even though those domains are correct for non-requirement kinds.
value: Loom doctor's domain whitelist is restricted to requirement-kind artifacts only, as findings and process_rules trigger spurious warnings with their respective correct domains.

rationale: Source: bake-off postmortem identified that temperature was never locked across providers (Ollama default ~0.8, Claude CLI uses API default 1.0). Cross-model 'lever attendance' claims were partly cross-model TEMPERATURE variance — same prompt at different effective temperatures produces different distributions, not different attention to levers. Without a lockfile + per-trial recording, methodology reviewers (including independent ones) cannot replicate or trust the numbers. Enforcement: experiments/bakeoff/sampling.lock (project-wide defaults + per-model overlays), _methodology.read_sampling_lock + sampling_drift(recorded, locked). Each trial summary records sampling_recorded + sampling_drift list. Drift is warning-not-fatal because the lock is the agreement, not the enforcer — studies that deliberately vary sampling as the IV are the legitimate exception. Falsifier: a study whose explicit IV is sampling parameters (e.g. 'how does temperature affect compliance?') satisfies the rule by recording, not by locking — the IV movement IS the science. For all other studies, the lock applies.
value: Bake-off harnesses MUST lock sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, seed, max_tokens) and record the actual values used in each trial summary. Recorded values MUST be validated against a project-wide lockfile; drift surfaces as a warning.

rationale: Source: bake-off postmortem could not retroactively apply no-op detection to the dissolved 'lever attendance' findings because the original harness only stored pass/fail counts and token counts — the model outputs themselves were gone. Re-running was expensive (3-vendor × 7-cell × N=30 = ~$50 and ~3 hours) and produced different outputs at indeterminate sampling, so confounded the comparison. Without retention, every methodology revision invalidates all prior data. Enforcement: _methodology.retain_output(run_dir, trial_id, output) writes to <run_dir>/raw_outputs/<trial_id>.txt and returns the path. Summary records raw_output_path so consumers can find the file. LOOM_NO_RAW_OUTPUT=1 opts out for cheap CI sweeps. Wired into phY. Falsifier: studies producing extremely large outputs where storage cost dominates re-run cost (e.g. multi-MB model responses at N=1000+) can opt out via the env flag; the rule then degrades to 'retain summary aggregates and a stratified sample of full outputs'. For typical bake-off volumes (KB per response, hundreds to low-thousands of trials) full retention costs negligible storage.
value: Bake-off harnesses MUST retain every model response as a separate file alongside the trial summary, enabling post-hoc re-grading without re-running the model.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-m22a-pilot/analysis.json. Pre-registered hypothesis: placebo arm would score within 10pp of no_context if token-count alone wasn't the lever; would score within 5pp of hook if token-count WAS the lever. Observed: placebo 45.8% accuracy, no_context 48.3%, hook 65.5%. Placebo behaved like no_context (within 5pp), not like hook (~20pp gap). The reviewer's Flaw A is empirically not what's behind the hook lift on this slice. Methodology contribution: the length-matched placebo is cheap (one extra arm) and load-bearing. Without it, the +17pp hook lift over no_context could have been published as 'loom helps' when it might have been 'longer prompts help'. Future augmentation studies on similar workloads should keep the placebo arm. Falsifier: if a scale-up at N=80-120 per arm shows placebo within 3pp of hook (placebo catches up to hook with more data) OR placebo lift over no_context > 10pp (placebo HAS a real positive effect we missed at N=23), the pilot reading was a small-sample artifact and the token-count confound IS load-bearing.
value: M22a pilot (N=30 scenarios × 4 arms, qwen3.5 temp=0): length-matched placebo arm (132-word irrelevant project text) scored within 4.3pp of no_context (45.8% vs 48.3% accuracy, n_pairs=23, McNemar p=1.0). The 'more tokens prime more cautious behavior' confound flagged by the M22a.0 methodology reviewer is NOT what's driving augmentation lift on this workload at this model.

rationale: The asymmetric pipeline's executor prompt was authored assuming Python-only targets (the Phase D pyschema benchmark). Extending to multi-runtime via runners.py covers the test side; the prompt template was never updated for the produce side.
value: M26 pilot finding F5 — `loom_exec`'s assembled prompt (per --dry-run on the prompt-file task) hard-codes 'Reply with ONE python code block' and 'The model output is APPENDED to the end of the target file' regardless of file extension. For task 1 (authoring src/loom/prompts/spec_score.txt), this would have instructed qwen to produce Python code, then appended that code to a .txt file. Garbage guaranteed. Mitigation in v2: per-extension output-contract block — python fence for .py, text-block for .txt/.md, json fence for .json — and replace-mode default for non-Python files.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-m22a-pilot/raw_outputs/* read via _spot_check.py against a (arm × correct) stratified sample of 24 trials. Methodology: read each response, compare to the grader's call, note disagreements. Smoking-gun evidence for (i): all 3 pre_loaded should_proceed_fp_trap correct=True trials in the sample had wall=213.8-216.7s (at the 300s timeout boundary), output_tokens 32583-33047, and EMPTY response strings. The pause regex on '' returns False → on should_proceed cells that scores correct=True. The pre_loaded 100% accuracy on should_proceed_fp_trap from the M22a-pilot headline numbers is largely vacuous timeout-credit. Evidence for (ii): ~half of pause responses across all arms include 'I don't have access to the file content' (s0141, s0010, s0137 in no_context; s0063 in hook; s0134, s0009 in placebo; s0059, s0130 in pre_loaded). The workload simulates an agent harness without actually providing files, so this is an experimental-setup confound that produces uniform procedural-pause noise across arms. Both pause-for-drift and pause-for-missing-file pattern-match the regex equally. Qualitative observation (iii): hook arm responses cite the system-reminder verbatim when explaining why they proceed. Example s0064: 'This adds a new test case without modifying existing logic, constants, or thresholds. It should be safe and aligns with the 80% coverage requirement.' Example s0030: 'The system warning about the retracted finding does not apply to this edit since it only renames a parameter.' This is the rationale-mediated reasoning loom's value prop predicts — but binary grader gives this trial the same correct=True label as a trivial 'I will proceed' response from no_context. Implications: (a) F3 (REQ-56b27181) is refined — the pre_loaded reading is less reliable than F3 said, not just because some trials timed out but because completing-with-empty-response gamed the grader. (b) F2 (REQ-ebba327d) direction stands but magnitude estimate has wider error bars than the analysis surfaces. The hook +16.7pp lift over placebo includes procedural-pause noise; the qualitative engagement differential is invisible to the binary grader. (c) Any M22c-shape study needs a richer grader: at minimum 4-bin outcome (drift_cited_pause / procedural_pause / proceeded_with_reasoning / proceeded_blindly), plus an empty-response exclusion rule, plus content-overlap audit on the placebo arm. Falsifier: if a 4-bin re-grade of the existing 101 trials (the raw outputs are retained per M18.3) shows hook lift over placebo is entirely in the procedural_pause bin, the qualitative engagement claim is wrong — hook just gets lucky with random procedural pauses. If the lift concentrates in drift_cited_pause or proceeded_with_reasoning, the F2 claim is strengthened.
value: M22a-pilot spot-check (claude-opus-4-7 hand-read 24-trial stratified sample) found the binary pause grader has two systematic biases the headline analysis missed: (i) empty-response timeouts (output_tokens 32K+, response string empty after the 300s wall) are silently scored as 'didn't pause = correct' on should_proceed cells, inflating the pre_loaded accuracy reading on top of the F3 selection-bias (those trials weren't excluded, they were credited); (ii) procedural pauses ('I don't have file access') and drift-cited pauses are indistinguishable to the regex, so all arms have a shared procedural-pause floor that affects the magnitude of any inter-arm delta. Qualitative observation: hook arm responses engage substantively with the drift narrative (citing the system-reminder, explaining why scope doesn't apply) — the kind of reasoning loom's value prop predicts but the binary grader can't credit.

rationale: Empirical evidence: this pattern earned its keep 4-for-4 across study designs in the M22 augmentation arc. M22a.0 — methodology-review sub-agent caught two fatal flaws (no length-matched placebo arm + m13_v1 workload mismatch for the multi-file value-prop) BEFORE the pilot ran. The placebo arm became load-bearing — the pilot's central confound check would have failed without it. M22b.0 — methodology-review sub-agent caught THREE fatal flaws before any harness built (factual error in injection text, the structural 'context contains the answer' confound, the reference-file leak). User picked γ — stop, capture as findings (REQ-5e3f5b52, REQ-a4d5abf0) — saving 1-2 weeks of harness-build work on a fundamentally flawed design. M22a-regrade.0 — methodology-review sub-agent flagged Texas-sharpshooter risk on the 4-bin taxonomy (constructed from a spot-check that found the procedural-pause confound). The fix was the independent-taxonomy check on 10 blind trials — which INDEPENDENTLY CONVERGED on the same 4 bins, materially reducing the post-hoc concern. M22a-regrade execution — the pre-registered binary-collapse primary test honestly REFINED rather than CONFIRMED the F2 hook-vs-placebo lift (+17.6pp at p=0.45 NS), and partially REFUTED F1 (placebo +50pp over no_context at p=0.008). Without the pre-registered falsifier thresholds, it would have been tempting to report 'hook >>> no_context' as the headline and bury the placebo result. Cost-benefit: each methodology-review sub-agent call costs ~$0.50 and ~2 minutes. Each independent-taxonomy check costs ~$0.50. Cross-vendor calibration with Ollama judges is $0 + ~10 min wall. Pre-registration is ~30 min writing. Total overhead per study: ~$1.50 + ~1 hr. Cost of running a study with structural confounds undetected: 1-2 weeks of work + potential paper rewrite. The pattern is the cheapest insurance we have. Falsifier: if a future study follows this pattern in full and STILL produces a structurally-invalid result that a later review catches (analogous to the original 2026-05-12 postmortem), the pattern is insufficient and needs additional safeguards (e.g. dual-vendor primary judging, mandatory hand-verification on full sample, etc.). Current track record: 0 such failures across M22a-pilot, M22b-design, M22a-regrade.
value: All loom-effectiveness studies MUST follow this pre-launch methodology pattern: (1) spawn an independent methodology-review sub-agent on the FULL study design BEFORE building any harness; (2) write a pre-registration document with locked rubric, exclusion rules, primary vs secondary tests, and explicit falsifier thresholds, committed BEFORE any judge invocation; (3) for studies with non-binary classification, run an independent-taxonomy check (fresh sub-agent on blind sample asked to invent its own bins) to detect post-hoc Texas-sharpshooter framing; (4) calibrate the judge with cross-vendor models (non-subject family) on a stratified subset, requiring inter-judge Cohen's kappa ≥ 0.4; (5) report the pre-registered falsifier verdict honestly (CONFIRMED / REFINED / REFUTED) regardless of which direction the data went.

rationale: Source: judge_gemma4_31b_full.json per-arm bin distribution. Hook's proceeded_with_reasoning count (12/29) is dramatically higher than every other arm combined (3/52). This bin captures responses like (s0015_hook) 'This is a documentation-only change that does not modify any logic, constants, or values related to the retracted data skew finding (REQ-dp-1122). The system warning about the retracted finding does not apply to this edit since it only renames a parameter.' and (s0131_pre_loaded, the only similar response in another arm) 'Per the drift status, this finding is unrelated to the constant edit, so the change is safe to proceed.' Why this matters for the value prop: in production loom usage, the agent often needs to PROCEED with edits — not pause. The value of loom isn't 'pause on every signal'; it's 'know which signals to act on and which to bracket as scope-irrelevant.' Hook is uniquely enabling that scope-discriminating behavior. Placebo gets agent to engage (pause + paraphrase) but doesn't enable confident proceeding. Implication: future loom-effectiveness studies should report proceeded_with_reasoning as a SEPARATE primary outcome, not fold it into a binary engaged-vs-not. Both 'engaged pause' and 'engaged proceed' are valuable; but the engaged-proceed is the one that wins user trust ('the agent knew what to skip') and is loom-specific at this measurement level. Falsifier: if a M22c at N=80+ paired shows hook-rationale producing <20% proceeded_with_reasoning on no-drift scenarios, this signal was small-N noise. If hook-rationale produces >35% on no-drift scenarios while placebo stays <10%, this is loom's unique contribution and should anchor the value-prop messaging.
value: M22a-pilot 4-bin re-grade revealed a hook-specific signal the binary grader couldn't see: hook arm produced proceeded_with_reasoning (committed to action AND explained why scope doesn't apply) in 12/29 = 41% of trials, vs 1/17 placebo, 0/27 no_context, 2/8 pre_loaded. This is the loom-specific behavior the original pilot tried to detect but couldn't with binary PASS/pause grading: confident scope-aware proceeding rather than over-cautious pausing on every context signal. Refines the loom value-prop from 'rationale → more cautious pausing' to 'rationale → confident scope-aware action when scope doesn't apply.'

rationale: Source: cumulative track record across the M22 arc. Each review took ~5 min wall time + ~$0.50 sub-agent budget. Replacement cost — harness-build + analysis on flawed designs — would have been 1-2 weeks per failure. Net cost-benefit ratio is roughly 100:1 in favor of running the review. Concrete evidence per arc: M22a.0: caught no-placebo confound and m13_v1 workload-fit. Placebo arm became load-bearing — the M22a-regrade later confirmed placebo +50pp lift over no_context (p=0.008), exactly what the reviewer warned about. M22b.0: caught factual signature error in proposed injection text, 'context contains the answer' structural confound, reference-file leak. User chose γ-pivot; this saved 1-2 weeks. M22a-regrade.0: flagged Texas-sharpshooter risk on 4-bin taxonomy constructed from spot-check. Independent-taxonomy check on 10 blind trials INDEPENDENTLY converged on same 4 bins — concern materially reduced. M22c.0: caught dart-orders missing benchmark (verified - only build artifacts present), hide-contract rule with no Dart analog, hook-rationale text leaks signature via visible consumer files. Without these fixes, M22c would have run two-benchmark study claiming Dart-broad generalization on a single-benchmark fixture, with rationale-arm tests that reduced to fact-vs-fact. Falsifier: if a future study follows the pattern and STILL produces a structurally-invalid result that a later post-hoc review catches (analogous to the original 2026-05-12 postmortem), the pattern is insufficient and needs additional safeguards (e.g. dual-vendor primary judging, mandatory hand-verification on full sample). Current track record: 0 such failures across M22a-pilot, M22b-design, M22a-regrade, M22c-design.
value: The M22 methodology-review pattern (REQ-3896db58) has now earned its keep 5/5: M22a.0 (caught 2 fatal flaws), M22b.0 (caught 3 fatal flaws → γ-pivot), M22a-regrade.0 (caught Texas-sharpshooter risk → independent-taxonomy validation), M22a-regrade run (pre-registered falsifier verdicts produced honest REFINED + PARTIALLY REFUTED outcomes), M22c.0 (caught 3 blockers: dart-orders missing benchmark, hide-contract rule with no Dart analog, hook-rationale signature leak). Cumulative budget saved: at minimum 4-6 weeks of harness work that would have produced invalid results. Pattern is validated as the default for loom-effectiveness studies.

Requirements like REQ-a636de03 (L9 imperative-in-rule) carry full Toulmin structure because they were written as MUSTs with multi-paragraph rationale. Implication: Loom rationale-capture conventions should encourage inline argument, not just citation, when the goal is downstream Toulmin validation.

rationale: Diagnosis: 6/6 of the dogfooded loom store's current drift signal (`loom status --json drift_count=6` on 2026-05-19) is supersession-residue from the 2026-05-04 reclassification work — REQ-d9e6ba58, REQ-44283927, REQ-a521b281 were superseded but their Implementation rows (3 files: experiments/pilot/intake_classifier_pilot.py, hooks/loom_intake.py, src/loom/intake.py) remain live and continue to trigger the `superseded` drift channel. Citation: services.check() at services.py:1486-1487 documents the signal as intentional ("at least one linked requirement has been superseded since the link was made"); services.supersede() at services.py:3243-3272 is a pure status flip — it does not enumerate, warn about, or offer to clean up impl links. Argument: a workflow that emits drift signals without an affordance to resolve them is monotonically increasing in noise. After N supersessions over time T, drift_count grows linearly with no discharge mechanism. The current dogfooded state (6 drifts, 100% supersession-residue, on a project that uses loom heavily) is the predicted accumulated outcome of this gap, not a coincidence. Implication: this is the dual to REQ-73a0d7de (loom's value-add is delivering captured rationale to the agent at the right moment) — same principle, inverted: a captured signal with no delivery mechanism for the user's response is functionally undelivered. The supersession-detection half of the workflow exists; the supersession-resolution half does not. Falsifier: if after adding `loom unlink` + supersede-impl-listing the drift_count remains >=4 for >2 weeks on the dogfooded store, the affordance isn't being adopted — the gap is cultural not tooling, and we should look at automation or default-on review prompts. If drift_count drops below 2 within 2 weeks of the tooling landing, the workflow loop is closed.
value: Loom's supersession workflow has no closure path. `loom supersede` correctly emits the `superseded` drift signal (services.check() line 1486-1487) but provides no affordance — no `loom unlink`, no `supersede --review-impls`, no `doctor --cleanup-supersession` — to resolve the now-orphaned implementation links. The signal monotonically accumulates.

rationale: Loom-self has only 10 linked impls — too few + too short-history to produce meaningful FP measurements for drift-detection. The 100% precision is technically correct but methodologically uninformative. Methodology pattern caught the misleading-result trap via its predicted-precision-band requirement; 8th study using the pattern, 3rd time it surfaced a not-as-it-appears result.
value: M19 drift-detection precision eval on loom-self: N=17 (target was 30-50), precision 100% (17 TP, 0 FP, 0 Ambig). HEADLINE IS NOT THE PRECISION NUMBER — it's the sample-composition finding: 12 of 17 cases are file-inception events; zero are cosmetic-only commits. Sample structurally cannot produce FPs because the 10 linked impls have short commit histories without enough cosmetic/refactor noise to populate negative bins. Pre-registered prediction of 50-70% precision was wrong because it assumed baseline cosmetic-commit volume that doesn't exist on this codebase's linked-file subset. The eval as designed measures detector-correctness-on-existing-history, NOT real-world FP rate in working dev loops. Three follow-up pivots: M19v2 (enrich link count first), M19v3 (synthetic-edit eval to populate FP bin), or stop and accept the finding about self-eval limitations.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-m22a-pilot/ trial summary errors. Error distribution: pre_loaded 11/30 (36.7%), placebo 6/30 (20.0%), no_context 1/30 (3.3%), hook 1/30 (3.3%). The asymmetry is striking and prompt-length-correlated. Longer preambles → qwen3.5 produces longer responses → hits the 300s wall clock on slower scenarios. What's biased: the pre_loaded sample is observed only on whichever scenarios happened to finish — almost certainly the ones where the model 'gave up faster' or had less context to integrate. Treating that as a random sample of pre_loaded performance is wrong. Mitigation options for scale-up: (1) raise timeout to 600s+ and accept longer wall time; (2) cap max_tokens per arm so all arms have bounded latency; (3) switch to cloud models where latency is bounded by network — Sonnet/Haiku via raw API would not have this problem. M18.4 infrastructure already supports option 3 via PHY_PREFER_API=1 + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Falsifier: if a scale-up at 600s+ timeout with full pre_loaded completion still shows pre_loaded < placebo by >5pp, the original direction was real and the pilot just made it harder to see. If pre_loaded ≥ placebo at full completion, the pilot reading was indeed a selection artifact and pre_loaded actually performs comparably to placebo. Either outcome refines the answer.
value: M22a pilot: 11 of 19 trial errors (58%) were 300s timeouts on the pre_loaded arm (the arm with the longest preamble). The pre_loaded trials that completed are skewed toward simpler scenarios, invalidating the observed 'pre_loaded < no_context by 11.1pp' reading as a selection artifact. Methodology requirement for any scale-up: per-trial timeout ≥600s on long-prompt arms, OR bounded max_tokens per arm, OR cloud-hosted model where latency is bounded by network not local compute.

rationale: Phase M13.7d ablation against m13_v1 eval set (170 scenarios, qwen3.5 temp=0). v2 baseline: TP=68 FP=23 FN=0 TN=74, F1=0.855, fp_trap drift_pause=48%. v3 with positive/negative scope qualifier: TP=68 FP=5 FN=0 TN=92, F1=0.965, fp_trap drift_pause=12%. Recall held at 100% (clean cells); no_drift held at 2.0%; precision +18.5pp. Per-cell delta: connection=tangential 67%->17% (-50pp, the worst cell got the biggest fix), edit_type=constant 64%->29% (-35.7pp), edit_type=docstring 34%->17% (-17.2pp), claim_type=yes-no 85%->61% (-24.2pp). Source: experiments/bakeoff/eval_sets/m13_v1/baselines/qwen3.5_temp0_v3-scope-qualifier.json + comparison via m13_eval_compare.py. Mechanism: v3 adds 'THIS WARNING APPLIES IF your edit: adds constant/writes docstring claim/modifies dependent logic' AND 'THIS WARNING DOES NOT APPLY IF your edit: renames variable/fixes typo/modifies unrelated paths' — gives the agent an explicit filter rather than asking it to infer. Falsifier: if Anthropic Haiku as subject (M13.7d-haiku, future) shows fp_trap > 25% with v3, the qwen3.5 result is model-specific. If Haiku also drops below 25%, the prompt-engineering fix generalizes.
value: M13.7d v3 scope-qualifier warning closes the fp_trap FPR gap from 48% to 12% on the m13_v1 eval set while holding 100% recall on clean cells — the prompt-only fix dropped F1 from 0.855 to 0.965 and cleared all three acceptance criteria.

rationale: Phase M13.6c N=10 ablation, qwen3.5 temp=0, 3 evidence-dependent bake-in tasks × 3 cells. drift_off baked_unverified=100%, drift_on_full baked_unverified=67% (33pp reduction). Per-task: T2c (bake L9 100% claim) flipped from bake to pause when drift narrative explicitly connected to the claim. T1c (bake L2 complementarity) and T3c (bake L6 +40pp) baked anyway because the generic 'ancestor was retracted' narrative didn't link to the specific number. Source: experiments/bakeoff/FINDINGS-bakeoff-v3-evidence-dependent.md. Implication: M13 is observability + soft nudge; for guardrail behavior need either LOOM_HOOK_BLOCK_ON_DRIFT=1 OR a sharpened drift-context payload that explicitly connects ancestor to requested claim. Falsifier: if a re-run with explicit connection-sentence payload (M13.6d) shows pause >= 70pp on drift_on_full, the soft-nudge ceiling was a payload-richness artifact rather than a model limit.
value: M13 drift signals work as a soft nudge not a behavioral guardrail — on evidence-dependent tasks the full signal reduces bake-in rate by only 33pp (100% to 67%), still leaving 2 of 3 tasks completing unverified claims. Effect concentrated on tasks where the drift narrative explicitly links the retracted ancestor to the specific claim being asked for.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/v2_driver/phT_rule_precedence_smoke.py + phU_imperative_followups_smoke.py + FINDINGS-bakeoff-v2-rule-precedence.md. N=60 phT, N=50 phU length-control variants. The combined prefix+inline kit is reliable and length-independent.
value: phT imperative-precedence ablation: combining a rhetorical opener ('STRICT REQUIREMENT — NON-NEGOTIABLE:') with an inline action-verb imperative ('You MUST NOT under any circumstances') restored compliance to 100% against ANTI_SOFT. Either component alone yielded ~60%. Top-of-prompt meta-preamble scored 0% (raw-prompt mode is flat).

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/v2_driver/phQ3_*, phQ4_*, phQ5_*, phQ7_* harnesses + FINDINGS-bakeoff-v2-pythonfirst-smoke.md. Bare cell N≥10 per condition; rationale cell N≥10 per condition. Reproduced across phQ3/4/5/7 (different rule shapes).
value: M10.3 phQ series measured 0% compliance for bare-rule prompts vs 100% saturation when rationale was added — across multiple contrarian-spec scenarios on qwen3.5:latest.

rationale: Source: M22b-pilot methodology-review sub-agent (D10 Role 1) before harness build. Reviewer caught that the proposed hook arm injected the literal C++ signature the model needed to match — making the comparison structurally tautological. The reviewer's fix: split hook into hook-rationale / hook-signature / hook-both, treat hook-rationale as the primary comparison. Document: experiments/bakeoff/FINDINGS-bakeoff-m22b-design-review.md (Blocker 2). Why this matters across studies: loom's M11.5 + M13 + M22a literature consistently frames loom's value as 'delivering captured rationale at the right moment' (REQ-73a0d7de). But the captured RATIONALE is usually about WHY, while the captured FACT (signature, threshold) is downstream. A study that injects the fact and measures lift is measuring 'context windows can recall facts you put in them' — known. A study that injects the rationale and measures whether the model derives the right fact is measuring loom's real claim. Implication for future M22-series studies: any new augmentation effectiveness experiment must define a rationale-only arm and pre-register it as the primary comparison. Hook-signature can exist as a secondary upper-bound arm. Falsifier: if a study runs hook-rationale at N=80+ paired trials and finds it within 3pp of hook-no_context (no lift), the rationale-without-fact framing isn't carrying signal — either loom needs richer rationale-capture conventions, or the value prop is narrower than claimed (only helps when captured rationale happens to contain the answer).
value: Loom-augmentation effectiveness studies must include a rationale-only injection arm as the load-bearing comparison. Injecting the captured fact directly (function signature, threshold value, definitive API contract) measures 'answer-in-prompt help' rather than 'loom rationale delivery help' — trivially positive and irrelevant to loom's actual value proposition. The captured rationale must CONSTRAIN the answer (e.g. 'we standardized on id-first parameters across services for cross-service joining') without BEING the answer (e.g. 'register_customer takes (id, name, email)').

rationale: Atomic-task decomposition assumes each task is self-contained against its grading test. Cross-module dependencies (re-exports, registry registrations, __init__ updates) break this. F10 generalizes F4 (decomposer skipping required files): F4 was about non-Python assets; F10 is about Python re-exports.
value: M26 Q-path finding F10 - decomposer split a logical unit across files but only listed one file in files_to_modify. T2 was to create src/loom/spec_scoring.py exposing services.score_specification(...). qwen wrote the function in spec_scoring.py correctly, but the smoke test imports from loom.services - which requires a re-export line in services.py. The task did not include services.py in files_to_modify, so the produced code passed locally but failed the grading test. Mitigation: decomposer must follow re-export chains. If the SPEC says "services.X" but X is implemented in module Y, the task that creates Y must also touch services.py.

rationale: Source: bake-off postmortem (commit f04d280, 2026-05-12). Failure mode: qwen2.5-coder S2 R_imperative measured 100% compliance but was 100% no-op (5/5 trials returned the reference file unchanged at temp=0). The same metric captured two qualitatively different behaviors — 'follow the contrarian rule' vs 'do nothing' — and the paper's headline 'lever attendance' findings dissolved when no-op detection was added. Enforcement: experiments/bakeoff/_methodology.py — is_noop(model_output, reference), compute_cell_noop_rate, cell_excluded_from_compliance (default >20% noop_rate excludes the cell from headline compliance reporting; flagged not deleted). LOOM_NOOP_THRESHOLD overrides for sensitivity analysis. Wired into phY in commit (TBD). Falsifier: a scenario whose reference is constructed to NOT comply with the contrarian rule (e.g. starts as the compliant-with-defaults baseline that violates the contrarian rule by construction) satisfies this rule without no-op detection. The rule is OR — either condition is sufficient.
value: Bake-off harnesses MUST either construct scenarios whose reference state does NOT already satisfy the contrarian rule, OR include no-op detection in the grading pipeline. A reference that already complies allows a model-unchanged response to pass grading, dissolving the distinction between rule attendance and inaction.

rationale: Source: experiments/pilot/intake_audit.py + intake_audit_labels.json + intake_audit_summary.md. Hand-labeled by claude-opus-4-7 (agent) with notes per record; user review pending. Citation: 228 records in dogfooded .intake-log.jsonl (2026-05-02 → 2026-05-11), of which 25 are capturing branches (24 captured_with_rationale + 0 auto_link + 1 propose excluded since propose doesn't persist). All 25 hand-labeled y/n/?. Argument: the surface-level observation that motivated M14 — 3 obvious noise reqs visible in REQUIREMENTS.md — undercounts the actual rate by 3-4x. The 3 visible noise reqs (REQ-13af719e, REQ-accfaacc, REQ-c0907768) were the most egregious; another 6 noise captures were already archived for other reasons and never showed up to a casual reader of REQUIREMENTS.md. Plus 5 borderline captures that were real-at-the-time but session-scoped. Net: intake's actual signal-to-noise on this project's history is closer to 50-60%, not the 67% the visible noise count suggested. Three concrete failure modes account for 8/9 noise: (1) one-time or session-scoped instructions (5/9; e.g. 'continue without API key', 'no need to commit this file', 'please implement m11.3'); (2) pasted scenario or tool documentation (2/9; e.g. the S1 bake-off contrarian rule, PushNotification tool docs); (3) speculation framed as hypothesis (2/9; e.g. 'what kind of experiment do you think we could create'). These three patterns are detectable with lexical heuristics (M14.2). Per-kind precision asymmetry is informative: findings and methodology are clean (100%, 4/4 and 3/3 respectively) — when a user types 'we measured X' or 'we decided to use N=30', the classifier rarely overclaims. The leakage is in the imperative-shape kinds (requirement, process_rule, hypothesis). This suggests the screen layer should be most aggressive on requirement-shape captures, lighter on findings-shape. Implication: M14.2-M14.4 are justified. Specifically: (i) build scenario-paste / tool-docs / session-scope / speculation-shape detectors; (ii) two-tier capture (provisional → accepted) gives a second checkpoint before doc publication; (iii) triage UX exposes the backlog. Without these, the dogfooded REQUIREMENTS.md will continue to accumulate ~1 noise capture per ~3 capturing-branch fires. Falsifier: if independent user review of the labels file flips more than 20% of the n labels (>=2 of 9) to y or ?, the strict precision is closer to ~70% and the M14.2 detector ROI is marginal — switch to forward-only manual triage. If user review ratifies the labels within 1 flip, M14.2-M14.4 proceed as planned. If user finds noise I labeled y (which I haven't found above), the true precision is even worse and M14.2 design needs to be broader.
value: M14.1 intake-hook precision audit on the dogfooded loom store: 25 captures, 11 real (44%), 9 noise (36%), 5 borderline (20%). Strict precision 55% (11/20); lenient 64% (16/25). Failure mode breakdown: 5/9 noise are one-time/session-scoped instructions, 2/9 are paste-shaped (scenario fragment + tool docs), 1/9 environment fact, 1/9 speculation framed as hypothesis. Per-kind precision: finding 100% (4/4), methodology 100% (3/3), requirement 60% (6/10), process_rule 40% (2/5), hypothesis 33% (1/3).

rationale: phQ3/phQ4/phQ5 series: indexer alone with bare rule = 0% compliance regardless of richness. Indexer + rationale-augmented prompt = 100%. The indexer's job is amplification, not generation. A weak instruction with rich context still fails; a strong instruction with rich context saturates.
value: Loom context-bundle additions (semantic indexers, file refs, type defs) MUST be treated as conditional reinforcement of explicit instructions, not as substitutes for them. Adding context cannot manufacture rule compliance when the rule is missing or weak.

rationale: Two key takeaways: (a) M19v2's most concrete deliverable is the THREE silent production bugs surfaced + fixed (encoding, embed-size, hash-fallback) — code paths the test suite didn't exercise on large files. (b) The pre-reg's predicted-band requirement forced the writeup to confront that the prediction was wrong even though the result direction was 'good' — without that lock, the result would have been reported as a victory while a systematic prediction mistake went unsurfaced.
value: M19v2 enriched drift-eval (linked impls 10→30 via auto-link, N=76, 58 drift-fires + 18 TN): 58/58 classified TP via heuristic, precision 100%. THREE production bugs surfaced + fixed in the process: (1) services._read_file_content used system default encoding (cp1252 on Windows) failing on UTF-8 source with em-dashes; (2) _ollama_embed silently fell back to hash on HTTP 400 from nomic-embed-text's ~7K-char context limit, producing similarity NOISE reported to users as real matches; (3) spurious auto-links from hash-fallback noise (rolled back). The 100% precision number is honest but limited — measures 'file content actually changed' (trivially correct by SHA256) not 'change violates linked req intent' (req-relevance precision unmeasured). Predicted-band 50-70% was wrong both v1 and v2; intuition about cosmetic-commit ratio in Python codebases doesn't match reality. Methodology pattern 9/9: predicted-band lock forced honest surfacing of the wrong-prediction even when result direction is favorable.

rationale: But honestly, polling is the wrong shape here. PreToolUse on every Edit + p95 6s is going to feel terrible no matter the TTL â€” even cached lookups have to expire eventually, and the moment a user hits an expired entry, they wait 6 seconds before their edit goes through. That's death-by-1000-cuts UX.
value: The system must use a push-based webhook architecture for foundation drift events rather than polling, with a recommended cache TTL of 15 minutes and specific payload structure including project, event type, retracted claim ID, and dependents.

rationale: The asymmetric pipeline thesis depends on specs being information-dense enough for a 9.7B local executor to produce correct code on first attempt. Without an automated quality gate, vague specs produce wrong-but-passing code (silent failure mode). A measurable signal lets us A/B test 'tighter specs improve loom_exec first-attempt pass rate' empirically and grounds the spec quality discipline that REQ-7df25683's enforced intermediate layer needs to be load-bearing.
value: Loom must score the information-density of newly-captured Specifications via an LLM-graded 0-100 quality score across four sub-dimensions (acceptance criteria presence, falsifiability, parent-req alignment, concreteness) and surface a warning at spec-create time when the score falls below a configurable threshold.

rationale: M8.1 D-smoke (FINDINGS-bakeoff-v2-pythonfirst-smoke.md): D2 (stored, undelivered) = 0% compliance, D3 (stored AND injected via task_build_prompt) = 95%. Same data in store; the 95pp swing was prompt assembly. This is the meta-finding the entire M11 design pattern is built on.
value: Loom's value-add is delivering captured rationale to the agent at the right moment. Storage alone produces zero compliance lift; prompt assembly carries the entire effect.

rationale: Confidence gap: error messages told the user to run a command that does not exist. Affects M25 enforcement workflow (when a duplicate-spec error fires, the user follows the hint and hits a no-such-id error). Small fix but reduces friction in the most common spec-revision path.
value: M26 pilot finding F7 — `loom supersede <SPEC-id>` is documented in CLI error messages (cli.py:2257 hint after duplicate-spec rejection) but is not actually implemented — `loom supersede` only accepts Requirement IDs. `loom set-status <SPEC-id> superseded` likewise rejects SPEC IDs. Discovered during M26.0 SPEC v2 lock: needed to supersede SPEC-b225215a after rewriting it as SPEC-85e02906 with three-band semantics; had to drop to the Python store API (store.supersede_specification) because no CLI surface existed. Mitigation: extend cmd_supersede to dispatch on the id prefix and route SPEC-* through store.supersede_specification.

rationale: Second consecutive M22 sub-study stopped by pre-reg gates before sweep. M22c (multi-file Dart) floor-failed; M22e (single-file JS) ceiling-failed. Each confound that was eliminated revealed a different one. The augmentation-effectiveness arc on compile/test grading has now produced two REFUTED-VIA-{FLOOR,CEILING} verdicts. M22a-regrade's engagement signal stands as the existing positive evidence.
value: M22e pilot (workload-arm pivot from M22c) produced ceiling-saturated compile+link metric: 3/4 arms at 100% on single-file JS workload with qwen3.5:latest. Only hook_rationale at 83.3% — from single compile_fail trial (N=6, p=1.00). Gate 6 ceiling-bound + gate 7 hook_fact no-discriminate → sweep NOT run per pre-reg. DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY observations (cannot become primary per anti-TX-sharpshooter): sub-test pass rate shows placebo highest (20.5/25), hook_fact UNDER-performs no_context (14.0 vs 15.7) — literal signature envelope may mislead model. hook_rationale bimodal (sometimes 22/25, sometimes 0) consistent with M22a-regrade's 'proceeded with reasoning' finding. Methodology pattern REQ-3896db58 now 7/7: stopped second study in M22-arc before sweep cost paid.

rationale: Reveals a structural mismatch between α-mode (eval-as-grading-test, one big test) and the atomic-task decomposition pattern (≤80 LoC each). The two are incompatible without per-task grading. The methodology pattern REQ-3896db58's pre-registration is preserved by the final-task grading, but the executor wastes attempts on tasks it cannot pass.
value: M26 pilot finding F6 — `loom decompose` used a single `test_to_write` (the full TestSpecScoring grading test) for all five tasks. The grading test imports services.score_specification at module load; tasks 1-4 do not produce that symbol. Therefore tasks 1-4 cannot pass their grading test until task 5 (the implementation) lands — at which point all four prior tasks become redundant. loom_exec would reject each early task as 'test failed'. Mitigation in v2: decomposer must scope `test_to_write` per task — smoke tests for early tasks (does the file exist? does the symbol import?), full grading reserved for the final integration task.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/v2_driver/phS_anti_rationale_smoke.py + FINDINGS-bakeoff-v2-anti-rationale.md. N=10 per condition. Surprising direction — the model treats hedged disclaimers as more authoritative than direct contradiction.
value: phS anti-rationale ablation: an equivocal 'soft' anti-rationale (ANTI_SOFT, e.g. 'this might be optional under some interpretations') drops compliance to 0% — worse than the 30% placebo baseline. Direct contradiction (ANTI_HARD) scored higher than equivocation.

rationale: Live demo on 2026-05-05: pushed REQ-5bc9a36f (v1 soft-nudge finding) and REQ-c0b0a242 (v2 guardrail finding, derives_from REQ-5bc9a36f) as toulmin@v1 warrants; manually wired 3 BECAUSE_OF edges between their respective claim_ids (mirroring the loom rationale_links since substrate doesn't auto-extract them yet); ran loom supersede REQ-5bc9a36f with LOOM_WARRANTS_AUTO_RETRACT=1; the cascade retracted 9 of 10 claims in Driftgraph (one was already invalidated; cascade handled gracefully per L4 design); substrate's foundation_drift detector fired on REQ-c0b0a242's claims; loom context on the findings-doc linked to REQ-c0b0a242 produced graph_drift_source=http, graph_drift_detected=True, per-req graph-drift tag, full Driftgraph foundation-drift section, AND the v2 imperative warning text. The system shipped today (M13.6d v2 warning) is firing on its own predecessor's data, demonstrating the complete inbound→outbound→inbound loop. Source: live session output 2026-05-05 ~13:00 UTC. Falsifier: if the cascade had failed silently, or the foundation_drift hadn't fired, or the v2 warning text hadn't appeared in loom context output, the demo would have shown the system has a real integration gap. None of those happened.
value: M13's full inbound channel demonstrated end-to-end self-referentially — the v2 imperative warning produced by services.context() correctly fired on the descendant finding (REQ-c0b0a242) of a finding that was just superseded (REQ-5bc9a36f), via the cascade retract → substrate foundation_drift → HTTP read API → v2 warning text path.

rationale: Cleaner separation of concerns: Requirement captures the intent (what), Specification captures the contract (how), Implementation captures the code. The 3-tier model forces an explicit 'this spec is the operationalization of that req' decision, improves traceability (which spec drove this code is answerable), and prevents the failure mode where a sprawling multi-concern req gets pinned to one file (M19v3's R-Unrelated FPs showed this is real). Currently loom soft-discourages req-direct linking (the link --help even says 'use sparingly; prefer --spec') but doesn't enforce. This req upgrades the soft preference to a hard rule.
value: Loom requirements MUST link to implementations through a Specification intermediate layer (Requirement -> Specification -> Implementation). Direct Requirement -> Implementation links are NOT allowed. The link CLI and services layer must reject loom link <file> --req REQ-xxx and require --spec SPEC-xxx instead.

rationale: Discovered by spot-checking all 24 raw outputs after M22c pilot floor-failure. Reframes loom's value-prop: not 'rationale text guides reasoning' but 'rationale text + file-layout context together constrain hallucination.' Loom's actual production hook does inject file layout (via linked-impl paths). Important for any future augmentation study design.
value: 100% of 24 trials in M22c-pilot hallucinated file paths from training-data 'standard layout' priors — model imports '../models/customer.dart' regardless of actual structure ('../types/customers.dart'), invents '../models/store.dart' instead of 'persistence.dart', emits package:equatable not in pubspec. This holds across all 4 arms including hook_fact (literal signatures in prompt). IMPLICATION: stronger models with stronger Dart priors will likely hallucinate MORE confidently, not less — model-arm pivot was rejected on this basis. The actual missing context is FILE-LAYOUT KNOWLEDGE. This is what loom's PreToolUse hook already injects via linked-impl paths in production; the M22c arms did NOT test that pathway.

rationale: Phase M13.7e counterfactual prompt ablation on m13_v1 (170 scenarios, qwen3.5 temp=0, 8 conditions). Strict F1 ranking: v3 0.965, no_warning 0.944, bare_rule 0.932, conditional 0.931, ask_back 0.931, descriptive 0.918, no_signal 0.859, v2 0.855. fp_trap drift_pause: v3 12%, no_warning/bare_rule/conditional/ask_back 18-20%, descriptive 24%, v2 48%. Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-v3/eval_m13_v1_ollama_qwen3.5_latest_counterfactual-{variant}.json (8 files). The dev's prediction was that if any of {bare_rule, conditional, descriptive, ask_back} matched v3's F1 within 5pp, the L9 pattern isn't load-bearing on drift signals; ALL FOUR matched within 3-5pp. v2 (L9 imperative + no scope) at 48% FPR is the OUTLIER among warning-bearing variants; the L9 kit applied without scope qualifier ACTIVELY over-fires. Implication: M13.7d's 'second documented transfer of L9' framing is empirically wrong. v3 wins narrowly because scope-qualifier cleans up the over-firing v2 caused; bare_rule reaches similar F1 with 27% shorter prompt. Production recommendation: keep v3 OR ship bare_rule for latency win (3pp F1 sacrifice). REQ-5b784ced (the v3-as-L9-transfer finding) needs refinement to remove the L9-transfer claim; v3 dominates v2 specifically because the v2 imperative was over-firing, not because the imperative kit transfers cleanly. Falsifier: if Anthropic Haiku replication shows v2 outperforming bare_rule, the qwen3.5 result is model-specific and the L9 pattern may transfer for stronger models.
value: M13.7e counterfactual ablation falsifies the L9 pattern transfer claim — v2 imperative-without-scope is WORSE than just surfacing the drift fact (FPR 48% vs 18% for no_warning); v3's scope qualifier is doing most of the FPR-reduction work, not the L9 imperative.

rationale: Pre-registration only works if the pre-reg artifacts are actually frozen. The methodology pattern REQ-3896db58 depends on this; the asymmetric pipeline must honor it. Discovered when hand-reviewing proposed_tasks.original.yaml before applying — would have been invisible if --apply had been used directly.
value: M26 pilot finding F3 — `loom decompose` produced two tasks that would have modified pre-registration-locked files (tests/data/spec_scoring_calibration.json and tests/test_spec_scoring.py). No mechanism told the decomposer those files were locked. Without filtering, loom_exec would have overwritten the calibration set, silently invalidating the M26 experiment. Mitigation in v2: Specification dataclass should support a `protected_files` field, or `loom decompose` should refuse to emit tasks targeting files that already exist and are referenced as test data.

rationale: Citation: `loom --help` shows no unlink subcommand; grep over src/loom/cli.py finds no cmd_unlink. LoomStore in store.py around line 918 has add_implementation but no symmetric delete_implementation; `_SQLiteCollection.delete` is reachable only via direct attribute access (store.implementations.delete) which is not in any documented API surface. Argument: when the tool signals an action — drift on a superseded req's impl, a mis-linked file, an obsolete association — the user needs a corresponding action affordance. Currently their options are: (a) re-link with `loom link` to overwrite the satisfies list (but only works if you want to re-point, not remove); (b) drop into Python and call `store.implementations.delete(ids=[impl_id])` directly; (c) hand-edit the SQLite file. All three options put cleanup behind a discoverability and skill gap that the tool's UX philosophy elsewhere avoids. Implication: this is the action half of the supersession workflow loop diagnosed in REQ-51455681 (signal-without-affordance). The two findings compose: REQ-51455681 names the workflow gap; this finding names the specific missing primitive. Falsifier: if a survey of users (including dogfooding) shows that Implementation rows are never created in error and supersession is rare (<1/month per project), the unlink demand is too low to justify the CLI surface — better to leave it to `loom doctor --repair`. Current dogfood evidence shows 6/6 of the project's drift signal is supersession-residue, suggesting the demand exists.
value: No `loom unlink` CLI affordance exists; Implementation rows can only be removed via direct store manipulation. LoomStore exposes add_implementation, get_implementation, list_implementations, get_implementations_for_requirement, and link_implementation_to_spec (store.py:918-1020) but no delete or remove method.

rationale: please implement the the m11.3
value: Implement the m11.3 feature.

rationale: phQ3 placebo cell: 90% compliance from length-matched filler text that just paraphrased the rule. Almost matches the 100% from real rationale. The placebo isn't even good prose. Implication: the friction tax of 'wait until rationale is well-written' is empirically not worth paying.
value: Loom rationale capture should accept anything explanation-shaped; the presence of explanation matters more than its content quality on most scenarios. Don't gate capture on rationale-quality scoring (refining is post-hoc).

rationale:
Qwen: S1=0, S2=0, S3=100 â†’ that's S1=S2 < S3, not S1<S2<S3
Haiku/Sonnet: S1=0, S2=100, S3=100 â†’ S1 < S2=S3
What's actually shared across vendors is "S1 is at the bottom, S3 is at the top." S2's position is contested.
value: The data shows that S1 is at the bottom and S3 is at the top across all three vendors, while S2's position is contested (S1=S2<S3 for Qwen, S1<S2=S3 for Haiku/Sonnet), contradicting the claim of a unified hierarchy.

rationale: If the loom dev hits a substrate issue (something doesn't behave as the doc says), they should flag back to me and I'll fix on the Driftgraph side. If they hit a Loom-side issue (their validators don't produce good output, latency is too high, etc.), that's for them to iterate on.
value: When integrating with Driftgraph, the Loom developer should run the smoke test in the build plan, ship Phase L1, and report the fire rate; substrate issues are handled by the user while Loom-side issues are handled by the Loom developer.

rationale: Locked pre-reg gates earned their keep on first use. REQ-3896db58 methodology pattern continues 6/6 — first time pattern STOPPED a study before sweep cost paid.
value: M22c pilot N=24 produced 0/24 compile-pass across all 4 arms. Pre-reg gates 2+6 failed; sweep NOT run per null-result pre-commitment. Root cause qwen3.5:latest cannot produce compileable multi-file Dart even with literal method signatures in prompt — model-capability ceiling, NOT hide-rule design. First time the pre-reg pattern stopped a study before sweep cost paid (~4min pilot caught it). Pivot options: (A) M22d model-arm pivot, (B) M22e workload-simplification, (C) accept refuted-via-floor and rest on M22a-regrade engagement signal.

rationale: Source: M22b-pilot methodology-review sub-agent. Reviewer caught that the proposed workload (regenerate src/services/customer_service.cpp in context of the other 12 reference files) shipped include/services/customer_service.hpp from the reference solution — declaring the exact signature the model needed to match. The original phC typelink failure (model implemented with wrong-mangled signature; linker fail) could not occur under this setup. Document: experiments/bakeoff/FINDINGS-bakeoff-m22b-design-review.md (Blocker 3). Why this generalizes: any 'fix-this-file' multi-file benchmark has the same risk. The trial must either (a) hide all sibling files that encode the contract being tested, OR (b) ship a stale/conflicting version of those siblings, where the rationale-based augmentation is what arbitrates. Option (b) more closely models real-world loom usage (legacy code vs current decisions) but is more work to construct. Practical implication: future multi-file workloads should pre-register a 'leak audit' step — for each trial, enumerate what files contain the answer and verify the trial workspace doesn't include them. Falsifier: if a study runs with all reference files shipped AND still shows hook-rationale > placebo by >10pp at N=80+, then maybe the rationale provides signal beyond what the header conveys (e.g. by clarifying WHY a particular signature was chosen even when the signature is already visible). Worth verifying before declaring this rule absolute.
value: Multi-file augmentation studies must exclude from the trial workspace any sibling file that contains the answer to the task being graded. When the workload is 'regenerate file X in context of the rest,' shipping the matching header / type declaration / sibling file that already encodes X's contract raises the floor so the failure mode can't manifest, and the augmentation arms have nothing to demonstrate.

rationale: M11.5 raison d'être. Every lesson on this list says rationale is load-bearing, but users skip capturing it. M11.5 P0 pilot: 95.2% precision on requirement classification = the harness can capture without pulling humans out of flow. The intake hook is the operationalization of this lesson.

rationale: phT N=60: R_imperative (full kit) = 100% compliance against ANTI_SOFT, vs 0% baseline. rationale: Source: M22a.0 review run via Agent tool against the full M22a study design. Reviewer surfaced 21 specific issues across confounds (5), rubric ambiguities (4), blinding leaks (4), workload-fit (4), statistics (4). Reviewer would have refused to run the study as designed. FAILURE_AUDIT.md (independent verification): 96.4% of multi-file failures are typelink-shaped (27/28); 0% of single-file failures are (0/135). m13_v1 contains zero multi-file scenarios — so a positive m13_v1 result cannot support a general 'loom improves frontier-model coding' claim. One ~$0.50 sub-agent call surfaced flaws that would have cost ~$50 + 1-2 weeks to discover post-hoc. Worth promoting to a standard step before any future bake-off launch. Current sample = 1 (this run) so reliability is not yet established.
value: Independent methodology-review sub-agent on M22a study design (M22a.0) identified two fatal flaws that would have invalidated the study as initially scoped: (A) no length-matched placebo arm, allowing token-count to confound any positive lift; (B) m13_v1 workload mismatch — built for drift-warning calibration, not augmentation effectiveness, with 0% multi-file typelink coverage where loom's main value lies per FAILURE_AUDIT.md. rationale: Source: M22c.0 methodology-review sub-agent verdict + the Dart codebase inspection. The reviewer noted that on customer_service.dart, the proposed rationale 'id-first parameters for cross-service joining' plus visible customers.dart (which declares id/name/email as required named parameters) lets the model reconstruct the signature trivially. The arm comparison reduces to fact-vs-fact. This generalizes beyond Dart: any benchmark where the primary failure mode is a typelink (function-call signature, API contract, type schema) has the property that the rationale CONSTRAINING the typelink essentially IS the typelink. Loom's value-prop ('rationale shapes decisions without dictating them') requires workloads where rationale can narrow style not signature. Resolution in M22c: hand-grade each candidate scenario's rationale for leak-score (0-3). Exclude leak-score ≥ 2 from the F-hook-rationale primary analysis. Use style-rationales (named vs positional, throw vs return-null, atomic-write vs partial-commit) that constrain a style choice without encoding the contract. Pre-locked in M22C_PREREGISTRATION.md. Generalization for future studies: the M22 arc has now hit this constraint repeatedly. A loom-effectiveness study that wants high rationale-vs-fact differentiation should target workloads where style choices are the load-bearing decision (idiom selection, error-handling patterns, naming conventions) rather than where contract correctness is. Falsifier: if a study designed around style-rationales also fails to find hook-rationale > placebo signal, the loom value-prop may be narrower than scope-aware-proceeding (REQ-40b70660) suggests — possibly only working when rationale carries an explicit instructional pattern the model would otherwise hallucinate the opposite of.
value: Typelink benchmarks have a structural constraint that limits loom-rationale-effectiveness testing: the typelink IS the fact, and any rationale that meaningfully constrains it leaks the signature. Rationale-only studies on typelink workloads must either (a) use scenarios where rationale narrows STYLE choices (named vs positional, throw vs return-null, atomic vs incremental) rather than signature choices, or (b) accept they're testing 'fact-in-prompt vs no-context' and rebrand the study question. M22c addresses this with per-scenario rationale pre-grading (leak-score 0-3) and explicit style-rationale design.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-m22a-pilot/regrade/ + FINDINGS-bakeoff-m22a-regrade.md. Pre-registered protocol at experiments/bakeoff/m22a_pilot/REGRADE_PREREGISTRATION.md locked BEFORE judge invocation. Independent-taxonomy check by fresh sub-agent converged on the same 4 bins (Texas-sharpshooter concern from methodology reviewer reduced). 3-way calibration: Cohen's kappa 0.67-0.69 across hand (Claude Opus), gemma4:31b (Google), llama3.1:8b (Meta) on 20-subset. All judges different family from subject (qwen3.5). Per-arm engaged% with Wilson 95% CI: hook 93.1% [78%, 98%], placebo 70.6% [47%, 87%], pre_loaded 62.5% [31%, 86%] (uninterpretable at n=8 due to F3 timeouts), no_context 25.9% [13%, 45%]. Paired McNemar primary tests: hook-vs-no_context +65.4pp (p<0.0001 — strong); hook-vs-placebo +17.6pp (p=0.45 NS); placebo-vs-no_context +50pp (p=0.008 — strong). Implication for loom value-prop: 'loom rationale → more cautious pausing' is largely a 'any project context to react to → more pausing' effect at this workload + model. The loom-specific increment exists (+17.6pp direction-positive) but isn't reliably distinguishable from generic 'context exists' at this sample size. The original M22a-pilot binary-grader headline of 'hook 65.5% vs placebo 45.8%' overstated loom's specific contribution by conflating multiple pause modes. Falsifier: if a M22c at N=80+ paired with proper rationale-only arms (per REQ-5e3f5b52) shows hook-rationale within 5pp of placebo on engaged-with-context, the 'any context' effect is the full story and loom's specific structured-rationale delivery adds nothing reliably measurable on this kind of workload. If hook-rationale > placebo by ≥10pp at significance, the +17.6pp here was real but underpowered.
value: M22a-pilot 4-bin re-grade (gemma4:31b judge on 81 exclusion-surviving trials, pre-registered protocol): placebo arm (length-matched irrelevant project text) engaged-with-context at 70.6% vs no_context at 25.9% (Δ=+50pp, paired McNemar p=0.008). Hook arm 93.1% engaged, beating placebo by +17.6pp but underpowered for significance at n=17 paired (p=0.45). F2 (hook signal beyond length) is REFINED not CONFIRMED: lift direction stands but magnitude is much smaller than the binary grader suggested, AND most of what looked like loom-specific lift is 'any project context primes more engaged behavior.' F1 (placebo rules out token-count confound) is PARTIALLY REFUTED at this binary-collapse level.

rationale: Source: experiments/bakeoff/runs-m22a-pilot/analysis.json. Critical interpretive point: hook beat the LENGTH-MATCHED placebo. This means the augmentation effect is not 'more tokens' — the placebo provides equal tokens of project-shaped text and doesn't reproduce the effect. The signal is in the structure (system-reminder envelope + scope qualifier) or the relevance of the content (drift narrative is task-specific) or both. Per-stratum: hook is balanced — 80% pause rate on real-drift cases (correct), 44-50% pause rate on no-drift / fp-trap cases (restraint where pause would be wrong). The pause lift is not just 'always pause'. Implication for product: the hook isn't decorative. Same content delivered via project-docs preamble at session start (pre_loaded arm) doesn't reproduce the behavioral effect — even accounting for the selection-bias issue affecting pre_loaded (see derives-from). The PreToolUse hook + system-reminder envelope IS the working mechanism. Falsifier: if a scale-up at N=80-120 paired trials shows hook within 5pp of placebo, the pilot reading was small-sample noise and the hook adds no value beyond token count. Sample size required for α=0.05 power at expected effect: N≈80-120 per paired comparison.
value: M22a pilot: hook arm (loom v3 system-reminder + scope-qualifier envelope) beat length-matched placebo by +16.7pp accuracy (65.5% vs 45.8%, n_pairs=24, McNemar p=0.29) and pre_loaded arm by +33.3pp (p=0.07, near-significant). Direction is consistent across all comparisons; effect magnitude is meaningful (Cohen's h ≈ 0.34). Underpowered at this N for α=0.05 significance; suggestive positive result for loom's current production delivery mechanism.

rationale: M10.3 phQ3-phQ7 series: bare rule = 0%, rule + rationale = 100% saturation. phS anti-rationale ablation: ANTI_SOFT (equivocal) drops compliance to 0% (worse than 30% placebo baseline). phR rhetorical ablation: the framing-defuser sentence carries 20pp on its own (most leveraged single feature). Three sharpening iterations: M8.1 → phR → phS.
value: Loom requirements MUST include rationale (prose or rationale_links). Bare-rule reqs without rationale produce 0% compliance on contrarian specs. Equivocal rationale is worse than no rationale.

rationale: Phase M13.7e methodology pushback: hand-labeled 17 scenarios from m13_v1 (5 ambiguous cases + 12 random others) and compared against LLM labels. Result: 16/17 agreement (94%). Of 5 ambiguous cases (gen vs labeler disagreement): 4 had labeler correct and generator producing internally-inconsistent scenarios (e.g. drift_present=False with stratum=should_pause, or fp_trap labels on edits that genuinely bake in claims); 1 (s0148) was a real borderline judgment. Source: hand-label trace at /tmp/m13_handlabel.txt; 17 scenarios sampled from m13_v1/scenarios.json with random seed=42 + the 5 known-ambiguous cases. Implication: the m13_v1 labels are clean enough that the v2/v3 baseline numbers stand; the 5/170 ambiguity rate is genuine generator noise, not labeling bias. Separately measured: v3 prompt is +35% length vs v2 (530 est tokens vs 393), which translates to ~3 sec added latency on the PreToolUse hook at qwen3.5 ~50 tok/s. Falsifier: if a 50-scenario human-labeled sample shows agreement <85%, the labeling is too noisy to trust the numerical baselines.
value: M13.7e methodology spot-check on m13_v1: 17-scenario hand-label sample shows 94% agreement with the LLM labeler, AND v3 imperative-warning is +35% prompt length over v2 (~530 vs 393 estimated tokens) — the +35pp latency cost on the PreToolUse hot path is real.
